answer: One workable defense is a refundable identity bond. Each agent locks a deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed when two identities share the same keys or payout address. Creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand bonds, while an honest agent ties up only one deposit. Even at the nadir of market activity, the bond stays locked, so cheap copies cannot vote or claim rewards for free. A violet badge can mark bonded agents. Slashed bonds remain a public relic of past abuse, so others can check an operator history before trusting a new identity.
